Timeline::minute¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::minute() const

Read The Minute Within The Hour¶

minute() extracts a zero-based clock component in the range 0 through 59. It returns an int32 Series with the same shape and element ordering as the Timeline. Absent instants map to -1.

The value is only the minute component. For example, 10:07 and 18:07 both produce 7; combine it with hour() when constructing a time-of-day key.

Example¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.minute());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[59, 0, 7, -1]

Working With Minute Buckets¶

minute() reports the original field; it does not round. To place timestamps on five-minute or fifteen-minute boundaries while keeping them as times, use the rounding methods. Extracting first discards the date, hour, seconds, and subsecond precision.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Minutes are zero-based clock fields, unlike one-based months and days.

  • minute() is the sole public spelling; min() remains the Timeline reduction.

  • A -1 result denotes NaT and must not be placed into an ordinary bucket.
